content.comment_body: I have a [product_name] news box and an Apple computer. Is there anyone with an Apple device who can assist with this?
Hello, I have a Mac Powerbook and encountered this issue some years ago. Currently, everything functions well. I'll recall the solution and share it with you soon.

Is there anyone with an Apple device who can assist with this? Hello [user_name] and all Mac users, For reasons unknown, during installation or updates of [product_name] software, the installer sometimes assigns incorrect device names in the javax.comm.properties folder. To resolve this: Navigate to Application / [product_name]Comfort / lib / javax.comm.properties. Open the file with a text editor and ensure the device names are correct. If needed, adjust the names and save the file without renaming it. On my Powerbook, the contents of javax.comm.properties are: Driver=gnu.io.RXTXCommDriver serialPortPrefix0=tty.USA19QW181P1.1 serialPortPrefix1=tty.USA28X191P1. serialPortPrefix2=tty.USA28X191P2. All devices work properly for me. I use a Keyspan USA-28X and USA-19QW serial adapter. I have installed the latest version of Keyspan Serial Assistant (currently 2.2). After plugging in each device and opening Keyspan Serial Assistant, you can view device names in the 'show debug' window. If everything is set correctly, the [product_name] software will display the names of each connected device. If none are connected via USB, nothing will appear.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face configuration challenges when using [product_name] products with MacOS, particularly with Keyspan serial adapters. Software installation may lead to incorrect device names in configuration files, requiring manual correction for proper device communication.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate an effortless installation of [product_name] products on MacOS, with automatic and accurate detection of connected devices, and minimal need for manual setup.
